chunks: From him, from Ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū al-'Abbās al-Baqbāq, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: 'In the broad/standard path (al-ṭarīq al-wāsiʿ), is anything taken from it if it does not harm the path?' He said: 'No.'

key_terms.الطَّرِيقُ الْوَاسِعُ: The broad/standard path or measure, referring to the standard quantity or weight used in commerce.
key_terms.يُؤْخَذُ: Is taken (passive verb indicating permissibility of extraction).
key_terms.يُضِرَّ: To harm or diminish (referring to the integrity of the standard measure).

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take a small amount from the standard trade measure if it doesn't reduce its value?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of deducting from a standard measure ('al-ṭarīq al-wāsiʿ') provided it does not compromise the integrity of the whole. This ruling addresses the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in trade, establishing that minor, non-damaging deductions are acceptable, thereby refining the application of fairness in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence.
